visualReview.notes: Every current standard frame inspected. Both south and west porch arches now open into the same recessed vaulted entrance, with the ceremonial inner door on the north. The long lancets, seven-light bands, roof dormers, four octagonal lanterns, open gilded crown, stayed flagstaff and flag remain intact in all turntable and close views.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Every current shared-material frame inspected. Metric sandstone and slate are coherent; small carved figures keep smooth vertex-tinted surfaces. Corrected dormers remain visibly recessed and corner tracery lies on turret faces. The changed entrance camera clearly shows both porch arches and the deep inner doorway.

geographicReview.notes: North-up placement matches the exact mapped tower body and octagonal corner projections. Published/current southwest views and the 1852 primary description establish the west/south open porch and north inner doorway, resolving rotation. The 98.5 m published stone tower plus 22 m flagstaff retains native dimensions. North/east Palace wings are separate architecture.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the complete detailed polygonal exterior. The published total and flagstaff dimensions, mapped body/turrets, current restoration-architect photographs and primary entrance account support the facade stages, lancets, heraldic friezes, porch, corner lanterns, mansard and iron crown. Carving and figures are original geometric interpretations; temporary restoration scaffolding and archive rooms are outside the permanent exterior.
